title: Strange Printer Problem

constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters.
content.inputFormat: Single line: JSON array of all arguments, e.g. [arg1, arg2, ...]

sampleTestCases.explanation: Print "aaa" first and then print "b" from the second place of the string, which will cover the existing character 'a'.

content.problemStatement:
There is a strange printer with the following two special properties:

* The printer can only print a sequence of **the same character** each time.
* At each turn, the printer can print new characters starting from and ending at any place and will cover the original existing characters.

With a string `s`, output *the smallest number of turns the printer needed to print it*.

**Example 1:**

```
Input: s = "aaabbb"
Output: 2
Explanation: Print "aaa" first and then print "bbb".
```

**Example 2:**

```
Input: s = "aba"
Output: 2
Explanation: Print "aaa" first and then print "b" from the second place of the string, which will cover the existing character 'a'.
```

**Constraints:**

* `1 <= s.length <= 100`
* `s` is composed of lowercase English letters.

solution.approach: Use interval dynamic programming. Let dp[i][j] be the minimum turns needed to print s[i..j]. Print s[j] separately after optimally printing s[i..j-1], giving dp[i][j-1] + 1. If s[k] == s[j], the print turn that eventually prints s[k] can be extended to also print s[j], so the interval splits into s[i..k] and s[k+1..j-1]. Take the minimum over all such k.

better.description: Interval dynamic programming reduces the problem to O(n^3) by storing the optimum for every substring and considering positions where the last character can share a printing turn with an earlier equal character.

optimal.description: Define dp[i][j] as the minimum turns for substring s[i..j]. Initialize dp[i][i] = 1. For each interval, start with dp[i][j-1] + 1. For every k in [i, j-1] with s[k] == s[j], merge the printing of positions k and j and use dp[i][k] + dp[k+1][j-1]. The minimum is optimal because an optimal schedule either uses a separate turn for the right endpoint or shares that turn with an earlier equal character.

bruteForce.complexity: Exponential time in the worst case; not practical for the constraints.
bruteForce.description: A direct search can enumerate possible printing sequences, but the number of sequences grows exponentially. It is only useful conceptually and is not practical for n up to 100.
